core_memory.travel_experiences: I've always been fascinated by exploring new places. As a fourth-year Computer Science major, I have to be strategic about planning my trips. With a packed calendar, I've managed to squeeze in some adventures that have given me some of my favorite memories.

archival_memory.sailing_trip: I took a sailing trip off the coast of Maine with a friend before my sophomore year. We spent a week exploring the coastal towns of New England. It was breathtaking. We'd wake up early, feel the crisp salt air, and watch the sunrise over the water. We'd sail past islands dotted with pine trees and have breakfast on the deck, planning our routes for the day. We had a local instructor who taught us navigation using modern technology and old-school methods with star charts. It was thrilling to disconnect from my coding mindset and focus on the wind, tide charts, and the synergy of the boat with nature. And I'll never forget the fresh lobster rolls we got at a small dockside shack – still the best lobster I've ever had.
archival_memory.japan_trip: I saved up money from my summer internship and went to Japan during my junior year's winter break. I was fascinated by Japan's blend of modern technology and traditional culture. In Tokyo, I explored Akihabara's arcades and electronics stores, feeling like I was in a futuristic wonderland. I tried to learn some Japanese phrases, but still ended up pointing at menus while ordering ramen. The food was amazing, and I was struck by the organized chaos of Shibuya's intersection. After Tokyo, I headed to Kyoto, which was a completely different vibe – calm and historical. I visited shrines and temples, and even spotted geishas walking down a side street in Gion. It was surreal. Writing in my journal, I described Kyoto as feeling like stepping back into an older era, where craftsmanship and tradition take center stage. The stillness and reverence left a lasting impression on me.
archival_memory.europe_trip: I went on a family vacation to Europe last summer. We flew into London and spent a few days exploring the city's history. We visited the Tower of London, the British Museum, and rode the London Eye. My sister was fascinated by the old artifacts and crown jewels. We also saw a musical in the West End, which was a highlight of the trip. After London, we took a train to Paris, where I experienced my first time in France. Although I barely remembered any French, it was easy to navigate the city. The pastries were a highlight! My favorite spot was strolling along the Seine River near Notre-Dame with a croissant in hand. It felt so relaxed compared to London. We spent a day at the Louvre, which was amazing, but even that didn't feel like enough time. You could spend a week there and still not see everything.
archival_memory.weekend_getaways: I've also done some smaller getaways with my roommates. We'd pack up the car with snacks and head to a state park or a nearby beach town on weekends. It was great to have some spontaneity and enjoy nature. One time, we found ourselves in a remote area with no cellphone reception, which initially frustrated us. However, it ended up being a blessing in disguise. We went hiking, told stories, and enjoyed the peace and quiet. It was a digital detox that recharged me for the programming tasks waiting for me back at campus. I realized how necessary it is to step away from my laptop and connect with nature every now and then.
archival_memory.future_trip: I'm planning a big trip before I graduate. I've been eyeing internships in Silicon Valley for next summer, which would allow me to explore the West Coast. I've heard great things about Portland, Seattle, and Vancouver – the coffee, craft beer, and scenery are highly praised. If I can line things up, I'd love to do a road trip through Washington and Oregon after my internship ends. It would be amazing to discover the coastal highways, Redwood forests, and hidden beaches. This might be my last chance to have a big chunk of free time before the post-grad grind starts.
archival_memory.travel_with_dog: I'd love to travel with my dog one day. I have a Golden Retriever named Archie who's super energetic. He doesn't do well with being cooped up in a car for too long, so we've left him with my uncle on our road trips. However, I dream of taking him on an RV or camper van trip, where we can go on hikes and beach runs together. It would be a different type of adventure, but it would create some amazing memories.
archival_memory.travel_values: Travel isn't just about checking off places on a bucket list for me. It's about experiencing different environments and learning from them. Japan taught me about reverence for tradition and efficiency, Maine showed me the timeless beauty of nature, and Europe opened my eyes to the depth of art and culture. Even short trips near campus help me unwind and discover hidden gems. I love collecting postcards along the way, which remind me of the vast world beyond my bedroom. Travel inspires me to explore new angles in my coding projects and research ideas. It heightens my curiosity and makes me want to discover more.
archival_memory.travel_future: I'm excited to see where my future career in computer science will take me. I hope to find a job that offers remote work options or flexible scheduling, allowing me to continue exploring. Whether it's a weekend trip to a nearby mountain range or a flight to a different continent, I'm eager for the next adventure. I'd love the opportunity to combine my coding skills with my love of travel, such as working abroad or collaborating on international projects. For now, I enjoy planning my next journey as a mental break from coding. It keeps me motivated and I'm thrilled for the next chapter of my life.
